home.title: One kit for Brazilian and LATAM ramps
home.subtitle: Take Brazilian reais on-chain through PIX, move value across the region, and cash out to local rails — with live quotes from competing anchors at every step.

onramp.subtitle: Pay in Brazilian reais, receive a Stellar asset in your wallet.

onramp.pixHint: Open your bank app, choose PIX copia e cola, and paste the code below.
onramp.simulateHint: Sandbox only: tells Etherfuse the PIX was paid.

onramp.done: Done — the asset is in your wallet.
offramp.title: Cash out to reais via PIX
offramp.subtitle: Send the asset back to the anchor and receive BRL in your bank account.
offramp.amountLabel: How much do you want to cash out?
offramp.signHint: Sign the transaction that returns your {code} to the anchor. The anchor pays the PIX once it lands.
offramp.insufficient: Not enough {code} in this account. Run the on-ramp first, or fund the account.
offramp.confirmHint: Sandbox only: tells the anchor the transaction landed.
router.title: One API, every anchor
router.subtitle: The same request fans out to every anchor that serves this corridor. Quotes come back in parallel and are ranked by what you actually receive.
router.noQuotes: No anchor serves this corridor yet.
router.skippedSummary: {count} anchor(s) could not quote — see why
router.apiHint: This whole table is one request:
sep.title: Speaking the standard: SEP-10, SEP-38, SEP-24
sep.subtitle: The table above uses unauthenticated SEP-38 prices — great for comparing anchors, but indicative. These three steps walk the rest of the protocol against SDF's live test anchor: authenticate, reserve a firm quote, then open the anchor's own interactive flow.
sep.step1Hint: The anchor issues a challenge transaction. We verify it server-side (right signing key, sequence 0, matching domains) before your wallet ever sees it, then exchange the signature for a JWT.
sep.step2Hint: With the token, the anchor reserves a real quote with an id and an expiry, instead of an indicative price that can move under you.
sep.step3Hint: The anchor hands back a URL and owns the KYC and payment UI inside it. Works identically against every SEP-24 anchor.
corridor.title: São Paulo → Mexico
corridor.subtitle: A full remittance corridor on a regional stablecoin: reais in, pesos out.
corridor.memoTooLong: Too long — accented characters take more than one byte.
corridor.swapSimulated: Simulated — no order-book path for this pair.
corridor.swapDex: Real path found on the Stellar DEX — this fills on-chain.
corridor.sendTitle: Send to your family in Mexico
corridor.sendHint: A single Stellar payment. Settles in about five seconds, for a fraction of a cent.
corridor.recipientHint: The recipient now holds USDC. The router shows who can pay it out in pesos.
corridor.payoutSimulated: Payout simulated — this anchor needs commercial onboarding.
corridor.amountLabel: How much do you want to send?
corridor.badRecipient: That is not a Stellar account address (it should start with G).
x402.title: Machine payments with x402
x402.subtitle: The same regional stablecoin, paying for an API call over plain HTTP.
x402.step1Hint: No key, no account, no subscription. The server answers with machine-readable payment terms.
x402.step2Hint: One payment for the exact amount, with the memo the server demanded. Settles in about five seconds.
x402.step3Hint: The same request, plus an x-payment header. The server verifies the payment on-chain — destination, asset, amount, memo — and serves the resource.
x402.replayNote: Try the same payment twice and the server rejects it — one payment buys one request.
x402.why: An agent buying a Brazilian FX rate should be able to pay in a Brazilian asset. The guard is asset-agnostic, so pricing an endpoint in USDC, TESOURO or any regional stablecoin is a one-line change.

onramp.duplicateHint: The anchor already has a pending order for this bank account and amount, and offers no way to cancel it. A different amount clears it.
onramp.amountAdjusted: The anchor already had a pending order for that exact amount, so this one was placed for {amount} instead.
onramp.depositHint: Transfer this amount using the rail below. The anchor releases the asset once it lands.
onramp.sandboxNoReference: The sandbox names the rail but does not issue a payable reference — there is nothing real to transfer to. Use the button below to tell the anchor the payment arrived, which is exactly what its sandbox settlement hook is for.
onramp.autoSettleHint: The sandbox moves no real reais — Etherfuse’s own payment-confirmation hook stands in for the PIX. Quote, order and on-chain settlement are real. With a production key, a real PIX payment triggers this instead.
